research_rationale: EO 5700 (August 31, 1931, Herbert Hoover) was read in full in the held Hoover Proclamations and Executive Orders compilation text (jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts/EO_5700.txt, Hoover PEO vol. II). Its single operative paragraph says Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 'is hereby amended so as to permit' Public Health Service officers to hold office in State, Territorial or local health organizations and State, Territorial or local health officials or employees to hold office in the Public Health Service. It has no own-terms end, date or condition that stops it. Executive Order 11408 (signed April 25, 1968, 33 FR 6459), a held Federal Register text, orders in section 1 that Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 'are hereby revoked' and in section 2 revokes all prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9, naming '5700, August 31, 1931' in the list. EO 5700 only amends Executive Order No. 9, so the express revocation reaches the whole order. The order is therefore ended on 1968-04-25. No earlier end is held: a search of the held corpus for the number 5700 found only this order's own text and EO 11408. Later orders that amend Executive Order No. 9 for other officers are not ends of this one. The OFR catalog search has a disclosed coverage limit (catalog starts 1937), which does not matter because the end found is later.
savings_reason: EO 11408 has only sections 1 and 2, both unqualified revocations, and no saving clause; EO 5700 only permitted officeholding, so no continuing command or accrued right is shown to survive.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end is held. EO 5700 has no own-terms end. The held corpus was searched for the number 5700 (cruden search, 2026-11-06) and found only this order's text and EO 11408. The amendments of Executive Order No. 9 by later orders (for other classes of officers) do not name or alter EO 5700. EO 9800 appears in the dossier chain only as a wage-control order and does not touch officeholding. The ledger flag FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT for EO 11408 is resolved: EO 11408 revokes Executive Order No. 9 entirely and names 5700 expressly, so the ending is whole for this order.
scope_check: One clause, the sole paragraph. EO 11408 section 2 revokes prior orders 'insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9'; EO 5700 does nothing except amend Executive Order No. 9 (permitting officeholding), so the revocation reaches all of it, not a part.
independent_command_check: No independent command: the order only amends Executive Order No. 9 to permit officeholding; it imposes no duty, deadline or separate continuing rule. Its permission rested on Executive Order No. 9, which EO 11408 section 1 revoked.
savings_check: EO 11408 contains no saving clause (only sections 1 and 2). Permissions granted by EO 5700 left no continuing command; no source shows any accrued right to be preserved.
